abstract: Background: REV-ERB nuclear receptors regulate gene expression and cellular metabolism, but their role in the response to hypoxia-associated stress remains unclear. We examined how the REV-ERB agonist STL1267 affects protein distribution and gene expression in HeLa cells exposed to cobalt chloride (CoCl2). Methods and Results: Immunofluorescence microscopy and RNA sequencing were used to compare vehicle-treated controls, cells exposed to CoCl2 plus vehicle, and cells exposed to CoCl2 plus STL1267. Representative images showed stronger nuclear HIF-1 staining after CoCl2 exposure. Nuclear staining was less pronounced with STL1267, while REV-ERB showed more extranuclear staining. CoCl2 exposure altered 267 genes, and STL1267 treatment during CoCl2 exposure altered 132 genes at a false discovery rate below 0.05. STL1267 increased ATF4 expression alongside genes involved in amino-acid synthesis and one-carbon metabolism, including ASNS, PHGDH, PSAT1, PSPH and MTHFD2. CTH and CHAC1 also increased, highlighting changes in sulfur-amino-acid metabolism and glutathione turnover. Among the genes induced by CoCl2, CA9, BNIP3 and LDHA decreased with STL1267, whereas HK2, PDK1 and VEGFA did not change significantly. Conclusions: STL1267 selectively reshapes hypoxia-associated gene expression and induces an ATF4-associated metabolic transcriptional program in CoCl2-treated HeLa cells, alongside qualitative changes in HIF-1 and REV-ERB distribution. These findings identify a potential connection between protein compartmentalization and metabolic stress responses, providing a basis for investigating how REV-ERB ligands influence cellular adaptation to oxygen limitation.
